questions.question: Which correction fixes the grammar in today's [EN] line: "this code dont work no matter what i try"?
options: A. This code doesn't work no matter what I try.
B. This code don't work no matter what I try.
C. This code not work no matter what i try.
D. This code doesn't works no matter what I try.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular needs doesn't (not don't). The main verb stays base form work. Capitalize sentence starts and the pronoun I.

questions.question: Which is the most natural English translation of today's [ZH] line: "看看当前codex的tts实现如何"?
options: A. Take a look at how Codex currently implements TTS.
B. See current codex the tts implement how.
C. Look codex now TTS implementation situation.
D. Check how is codex TTS doing implement.
questions.explanation: 看看 means review or take a look. 当前 is currently. 如何 asks how something is done — option A is a natural technical request.

questions.question: In today's log you discussed a "quality gate" for SenseVoice ASR (CER must pass before replacing the default). What does "gate" mean here?
options: A. A checkpoint that must be passed before moving to the next stage.
B. A physical barrier on the RK3576 board.
C. A Git branch protection rule.
D. A type of neural network layer.
questions.explanation: In engineering, a gate is a go/no-go checkpoint — e.g., CER must meet the baseline before production migration is allowed.

questions.question: Which English best translates today's [ZH] suggestion: "用worktree吧"?
options: A. Let's use worktrees.
B. Use the work tree please.
C. We should working tree it.
D. Put it in worktree folder now.
questions.explanation: 吧 softens a suggestion. Git worktree lets multiple branches be checked out in separate directories — Let's use worktrees is natural when proposing that workflow.

questions.question: Which version correctly punctuates and capitalizes today's [EN] questions about runtime: "What's the memory usage? What's the execution flow? is it running on NPU/CPU?"
options: A. What's the memory usage? What's the execution flow? Is it running on NPU/CPU?
B. What's the memory usage? What's the execution flow? is it running on NPU/CPU?
C. What's the memory usage, what's the execution flow, is it running on NPU/CPU
D. What's the memory usage? What's the execution flow? Is it running on npu/cpu?
questions.explanation: Each question is a separate sentence and must start with a capital letter. NPU and CPU are acronyms and stay uppercase.

questions.question: Which English question best translates today's [ZH] line: "我们的ASR目标到底是啥"?
options: A. What exactly is our ASR goal?
B. Our ASR target is what thing?
C. What ASR aim we have finally?
D. Which is our ASR purpose actually mean?
questions.explanation: 到底 adds emphasis — what exactly or ultimately. 啥 is informal for 什么 (what). Option A captures the direct, goal-clarifying tone.

questions.question: Translate into natural English: "先写TTS的优化方案, 然后,我们再写一个ASR的方案, 两者并行执行"
questions.modelAnswer: First write the TTS optimization plan, then we'll write an ASR plan, and execute both in parallel.
questions.explanation: 先…然后 structures the sequence of planning. 两者并行执行 means the two tracks run at the same time after their plans are drafted.

questions.question: Rewrite today's [EN] line with correct grammar and capitalization: "this code dont work no matter what i try"
questions.modelAnswer: This code doesn't work no matter what I try.
questions.explanation: Use doesn't for third-person singular. No matter what I try is a fixed phrase meaning every attempt fails.

questions.question: Translate into natural English: "没有别的地方需要优化了吗"
questions.modelAnswer: Isn't there anywhere else that needs optimization?
questions.explanation: 没有别的地方 means no other places or areas. 了吗 turns it into a question checking whether optimization is complete.

questions.question: Write a natural English message asking a teammate to commit finished TTS work, based on today's [ZH] line: "TTS那边都写完了, 代码帮他提交吧"
questions.modelAnswer: TTS is done on their side — please commit the code for them.
questions.explanation: 那边 refers to the other person's workstream. 帮他提交 means submit or commit on their behalf, common when coordinating parallel agent tasks.
